stem: A 16-year-old reports several sexual partners over a short period and says condoms are used inconsistently. What is the best focus for follow-up?

options.text: Reassure the adolescent that this is normal experimentation and does not need further discussion
Focus only on how the adolescent feels after sex and avoid discussing pregnancy or STI risk
Broaden counselling and follow-up because the pattern suggests risky sexual behaviour with unplanned pregnancy and STI risk
Avoid further sexual health discussion unless the adolescent develops STI symptoms
Conclude that social media is the main issue rather than sexual health risk

explanation: Broaden counselling and follow-up. This pattern suggests risky sexual behaviour, so the discussion should include unplanned pregnancy and STI risk rather than reassurance alone.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Multiple partners over a short period and inconsistent condom use are markers of risky sexual behaviour. Follow-up should address both STI prevention and unplanned pregnancy risk. This should not be dismissed as ordinary experimentation when the risk pattern is clear.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because this pattern fits risky sexual behaviour and needs further sexual health discussion.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because emotional wellbeing matters, but pregnancy and STI risk also need to be addressed.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because the pattern suggests risky sexual behaviour linked to unplanned pregnancy and STI risk.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because sexual health counselling should not wait for symptoms to appear.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because social media is not the main issue; the concern is the sexual risk pattern described.
